modules.egg-analysis.stereo_defaults_to_: Stereo defaults to EGG on the left and audio on the right; channels can be swapped. Each channel is independently normalized to a peak of 0.7. Analysis starts automatically after loading. View CQ/SQ and the spectrogram on the left; click a curve to set the microscopic centre on the right. Within any of the four plots, use the wheel to zoom and drag to pan. Large windows need no outer scrolling; small windows allow scrolling. After focusing, use arrow keys to pan and +/− to zoom; dragging updates live. The microscopic window supports 5–5000 ms. Wide views retain the legacy subsampled display and event positions. Click the bottom overview to move the selection while retaining its duration, clamping at the end. Drag to choose another interval and release to update. Only the latest selection is kept during continuous interaction. Interactive previews remain in memory and are excluded from processing records.
modules.egg-analysis.defaults_gci_slope_: Defaults: GCI slope, GOI scale 0.25, high-pass 25 Hz, low-pass 2000 Hz. Automatic peak detection uses 200 ms windows with 100 ms steps and threshold max(0.01, 0.6 × local absolute peak), affecting peaks only. Valley prominence 0.01 is a manually adjustable starting point; inspect false and missed detections. Automatic dB sets the upper bound to the actual maximum PSD at 0–5000 Hz in the current selection, displaying 50 dB below it. Enabled by default, its colour scale keeps updating after panning or zooming. The checkmark, button background, and status indicate whether it is enabled. Disable it for manual adjustment. Silent intervals keep the current finite colour scale and show a notice. Analysis parameter changes update automatically; retry the preview if reading fails. Missing CQ/SQ values remain blank independently.
modules.egg-analysis.saving_csv_three_pl: Saving CSV / three plots creates a complete export task for the current selection. View it in processing records when complete; select a save folder on desktop or download files individually on the web. Praat AC and REAPER extract F0 from the audio channel using the shared F0 bounds on the left, defaulting to 30–800 Hz at 10 ms steps. Changing bounds reruns detection; bounds are saved with parameter drafts and single-file exports. GCI F0 remains derived from EGG events and is unaffected by these search bounds. Single-file CSV always retains Praat and GCI, adding REAPER columns when selected. Batch parameters are saved independently and retain both F0 types by default. The 20 ms mean absolute amplitude silence mask on the complete filtered file affects CSV only.
modules.egg-analysis.inverse_filtering_s: Inverse filtering suits stable vowel segments and is limited to 10 seconds / 960000 frames. Longer selections still use one set of mean LPC coefficients; shorten the selection when the vocal tract changes. Results open automatically and can be saved as PNG in 6 / 4 / 4 / 2 plot layouts. Output includes normalized analysis audio and the V2 simplified inverse-filter estimate, using a fixed 3 ms segment after GCI without verifying the closed phase against GOI. A single analysis file is limited to 30 minutes / 2 GB. Long files use chunked processing; the live macroscopic view is limited to 60 seconds. The overview uses lightweight display data, while playback and computation retain the original sample rate. Use the separate button for full exports. Live F0 for long files is estimated and cached in the current view; GCI F0 outliers are evaluated against that view. Full exports use the whole-file event grid, so edge handling and outlier filtering may differ. Microscopic waveforms, events, and CQ retain the legacy local filtering ranges. Hover over the four plots for provenance: CQ uses repeated filtering of processed ±100 ms; the microscopic display filters and crops raw ±100 ms; events use raw ±50 ms. GCI is solid and GOI dashed.
